title: Publish Settings 'JPEG quality' slider is ignored — never reaches compileDocument
description:
EDITOR-ONLY GAP (proactive QA). The Publish Settings dialog exposes a JPEG quality slider (1-100, default 80) but the value is stored/persisted only and NEVER affects the published SWF. Photo bitmaps are emitted by passing the library dataUri's original JPEG bytes through verbatim, so changing the slider produces a byte-identical SWF for photo content.

This is the same gap class as distort-warp / component-params / filter-drop: a setting visible in the UI that has no consumer in the compile path. It directly violates task 0741's acceptance criterion 'JPEG quality slider changes the encoded JPEG size of a bitmap-containing SWF' — 0741 is marked done but this criterion was never met.

## Evidence (HEAD 1dbebbb89fcb15f3d768e5e911573eab274b4086)

Dialog exposes the slider:
- packages/authoring-ui/src/PublishSettingsDialog.tsx:357 useState(activeSettings.jpegQuality)
- :762-776 the range input <input type=range min=1 max=100 value={jpegQuality}>
- :373 included in currentFieldsAsSettings() and persisted to the profile / doc.publishProfiles

But it is NOT wired to compile:
- packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx:2505-2511 usePublish(doc, {...}) passes ONLY compress, protect, debugPassword. jpegQuality is absent.
- packages/swf/src/compiler/options.ts CompileOptions has NO jpegQuality / bitmapQuality field at all.
- grep 'jpegQuality|quality' over packages/swf/src returns zero compiler consumers (only filter.quality and _quality stage actions, unrelated).
- packages/swf/src/compiler/characters.ts:140-164 photo bitmaps: rawBytes = dataUriToBytes(bitmapItem.dataUri); imageBytes = ensureJpegEOI(rawBytes); ... writeTag(DefineBitsJPEG2, imgPayload) — original bytes passed through, never re-encoded. No quality param anywhere in the path.

## Verified working (no defect) — same QA pass
- Compress movie -> CWS vs FWS: swf-dump confirmed FWS (compress:false) vs CWS (compress:true), CWS decompresses cleanly. Shell wires it.
- Protect from import -> Protect tag (24) emitted. Verified by raw tag decode.
- Debugging permitted + password -> EnableDebugger2 (64) body contains the password + DebugId (63). Verified by raw tag decode.
- Width/Height -> header RECT (800x600 -> 16000x12000 twips; 320x240 -> 6400x4800). Verified swf-dump.
- Frame rate -> header frameRate (24.0 / 12.0). Verified swf-dump.
- Background color -> SetBackgroundColor tag (r255 red / g255 green). Verified swf-dump.
- SWF version -> hardcoded 8 in writer.ts:70; dialog shows it read-only ('SWF v8'). Consistent.
- HTML tab options (publishHtml/quality/wmode/scale/loop/menu) feed the HTML wrapper (packages/swf/src/html.ts), not the SWF — correct by design.

## Fix options
1. Add jpegQuality (or bitmapQuality) to CompileOptions; thread it from Shell.tsx:2505 usePublish call. In characters.ts photo path, re-encode the decoded ARGB pixels (already available in options.bitmapPixels for transparent photos) to JPEG at the requested quality instead of passing dataUri bytes through. Note: re-encoding needs a JPEG encoder in the compile path (none today) — non-trivial.
2. OR, if per-asset quality (task 0812 Bitmap Properties) is the intended single source of truth, REMOVE the global slider from PublishSettingsDialog to stop implying it does something, and document that document-level JPEG quality is not supported.

## Acceptance
A bitmap-containing doc published at jpegQuality 20 vs 90 must produce different DefineBitsJPEG2/3 payload bytes (smaller at lower quality), OR the slider is removed. swf-dump byte comparison of the photo tag payload is the oracle.
